principles: Owner lease core should remain host-neutral and consume a canonical Lattice identity contract.
Host adapters own host-specific session discovery and bridging.
ppid-derived identity must be treated as degraded fallback for owner-gated mutations.
Documentation must distinguish local coordination identity from Authority or cryptographic identity.
drivers: Parallel story development must not self-block when shell parent processes change.
Future hosts should have one onboarding rule instead of repeated core changes.
The first deliverable is an execution plan reviewed by two hosts, not runtime code.

options.name: A: Canonical LATTICE_SESSION_ID adapter contract
pros: Keeps owner lease core stable and host-neutral
Gives Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity/agy, and future hosts one onboarding rule
Allows wrappers and dispatch to bridge or generate stable session ids without changing core each time
cons: Requires adapter/wrapper updates before full runtime protection exists
Requires migration guidance for existing CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID fallback

options.name: B: Add every host-specific env variable directly to owner lease core
pros: Fastest local patch for Codex and Antigravity if their env names are known
cons: Future hosts require core edits and new risk each time
Makes core responsible for host runtime discovery instead of owner lease semantics

options.name: C: Keep current behavior and document users should set LATTICE_SESSION_ID manually
pros: No code changes needed after the document
Users can work around ppid instability immediately
cons: Operationally fragile for automated parallel dispatch
Does not protect default Codex/agy workflows
Leaves the same failure mode to appear under host scheduler changes

rationale: Choose the canonical adapter contract because owner lease is a core concurrency primitive and should not depend on each host runtime implementation detail. Wrappers and dispatch are the correct layer to translate native session facts into LATTICE_SESSION_ID.

preMortem.scenario: A future host is added without setting LATTICE_SESSION_ID
preMortem.trigger: New host integration calls mutating Lattice commands but only exposes host-specific session env
preMortem.consequence: Owner lease falls back to ppid and may self-reject across command invocations
preMortem.mitigation: Execution plan requires host onboarding checklist and smoke test that stable host session bridges into LATTICE_SESSION_ID before owner-gated commands

preMortem.scenario: ppid fallback remains silent on owner-gated mutation
preMortem.trigger: No stable session env is available in Codex/agy or a manual terminal
preMortem.consequence: The system appears to work until process-parent behavior changes, then creates false foreign leases
preMortem.mitigation: Plan requires warning or eventual fail-closed policy for derived-ppid on owner-gated mutating commands while preserving read-only diagnostics

preMortem.scenario: The contract is confused with Authority identity
preMortem.trigger: Documentation uses identity/security language too strongly
preMortem.consequence: Users over-trust local session ids as authentication or production authority evidence
preMortem.mitigation: Plan explicitly states LATTICE_SESSION_ID is local coordination only, forgeable, non-cryptographic, and never Authority receipt evidence

preMortem.scenario: Two-host review is recorded as prose only
preMortem.trigger: Reviewers comment in chat but no durable evidence path is defined
preMortem.consequence: Implementation proceeds without auditable independent review
preMortem.mitigation: Plan requires reviewer evidence through Lattice review/finding/pass or host verdict events with material binding
